To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the olfactory system of Drosophila utilizes multiple signaling mechanisms, and that some of these mechanisms evolved relatively late in insect evolution.

1) Drosophila olfactory receptors are activated by a diverse array of signaling mechanisms, 2) some olfactory receptor families are activated by mechanisms that have not been observed before in other organisms, 3) some odorants activate olfactory receptors through multiple mechanisms, 4) odorants that activate the same receptor can be detected by distinct mechanisms, and 5) odorants that do not activate the same receptor are detected by the same signaling mechanisms.
Drosophila olfactory neurons express a variety of receptors that are activated by diverse signaling mechanisms, some of which may be unique to the insects.

understanding how animals perceive and respond to their environment.
understanding the mechanisms of olfactory signal transduction in Drosophlia.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie odorant detection and signal transduction in the olfactory system.

insects are the most diverse group of animals on Earth and that they have evolved a diverse set of mechanisms to detect volatile odorants.
